statement0:
The word "decreased" is mentioned two or more times in 23.7% of neuroscience papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "decreased" , 33.1% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a somewhat lower rate than the median Psychology paper (median shown in black); relative to other words, papers with "decreased" are in the bottom 37th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better).
Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability.
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "decreased" tend to be published in lower impact factor journals (7th percentile among all words) but tend to be cited more (84th percentile word). In general, this word is negatively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are less likely to publish papers containing "decreased" (6th percentile).
